subject: VPC upgrade curation & failsafe brief
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, infraops@acmecloud.com
Cc: jane.doyle@networksrus.com
Date: Tue, 02 Jun 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: VPC upgrade curation & failsafe brief

Team / InfraOps,

I'm sharing a compact brief for the upcoming Private deployment patch wave (v2026.06.*). Goal: get alignment on the curation rules, version-pinning policy, maintenance windows, and the concrete rollback triggers we will hand to AcmeCloud ops. This is intentionally short — details are in the attached runbook. Please scan and call out any missing failure modes by EOD tomorrow.

Key points:
- Version curation: we will pin customer fleets to the nearest tested minor (e.g., 1.14.x) and allow a single hotpatch channel (1.14.1x) for critical fixes only. No automatic bumping across minor versions during the window.
- Maintenance window: target UTC 02:00-06:00 (US-West preferred). We propose a 2-hour per-pod adjustable slice with a global soft-window of 4 hours for stragglers.
- Canary plan: 3-stage canary (10% -> 30% -> 100%) per-AZ with health gates (error-rate, p99 latency, KV cache hit ratio). Canary duration per stage: 20 minutes, then observation.
- Rollback triggers (high level): sustained p99 latency increase > 250ms vs baseline for 5 minutes, or error-rate > 3% for 3 minutes, or any unrecoverable pin conflicts (dep graph mismatch).
- Net quiesce: we will run a net-quiesce prior to slice cutover to drain in-flight long-lived streams and checkpoint KV caches. See checklist attached.

Attachments: upgrade_runbook_v2.pdf (full playbook), net-quiesce-checklist.md.

Asks:
1) Karthik — confirm kernel/driver gating we discussed for the NVMe firmware irregularities; if we cannot avoid the firmware bump we should add a hardware-compatibility gate.
2) Neha — can you validate the canary metrics & proposed thresholds against our telemetry for AcmeCloud?
3) Laura — if we get these gates and the schedule, can we lock the customer-facing comms and SLA exceptions?

I'll sync with Acme infraops in the afternoon to confirm their availability.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Sr. Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, infraops@acmecloud.com
Cc: jane.doyle@networksrus.com
Date: Tue, 02 Jun 2026 13:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VPC upgrade curation & failsafe brief

Thanks Alex — good concise brief. A few technical clarifications and one small ask:

1) NVMe/driver gating: I agree we should avoid firmware bumps during the slice unless it's emergency-only. If Acme insists, we must run a hardware compatibility sweep on the canary hosts first. I'll add a short script to the runbook to assert expected firmware versions and fail the stage if mismatch > 5% of hosts.

2) KV cache checkpointing: we need to snapshot and push KV cache checkpoints to object storage prior to node reboots for quick warm starts. I've added a step to the runbook (see upgrade_runbook_v2.pdf, section 3.2). If checkpoint push fails, the node should be marked for manual review and the slice should pause.

3) Canary metrics: Neha, the p99 baseline numbers in Acme are slightly higher during backup windows — we should factor an adaptive baseline that ignores their nightly backup surge. Otherwise the rollback gates will be too aggressive.

4) Rollback automation: propose an automated staging rollback for the 10% -> 30% transition (i.e., auto-revert that slice if gates fail). For full fleet rollback we keep manual approval but provide a one-click revert on the dashboard. This reduces blast radius.

5) Network quiesce: Jane — can you confirm that your team can perform the two-step quiesce (TCP drain then graceful LB flip) in the 5-minute window we allocate per node? If not, we should extend the slice time.

I'll push a small patch to the runbook and attach a canary-slice-matrix.csv for the proposed thresholds.

-Karthik
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, infraops@acmecloud.com
Date: Wed, 03 Jun 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VPC upgrade curation & failsafe brief

Quick check from telemetry side — I've run the proposed thresholds against the last 30 days for Acme's cluster. Summary attached (canary-slice-matrix.csv). Highlights:
- Baseline p99: 180ms median, spikes to ~310ms during their nightly backups (00:30-01:15 UTC). We should shift our canary window to start after their backup or use the adaptive baseline Karthik mentioned.
- KV hit ratio: healthy at 88-92% normally; slices that cause warm restarts drop to ~65% for ~6–8 minutes. Pin policy must account for that transient expense.
- Error-rate: steady under 0.6% except for one incident (third-party auth flake) that spiked to 2.4% for 4 minutes last month. This would have tripped the proposed 3% gate — we are safe, but consider a short cooldown before auto-revert to avoid chasing transient third-party blips.

Recommendation:
- Move our big fleet canary to start at 02:30 UTC to avoid backup noise.
- Implement a 3-minute cooldown window before auto-revert of a slice to allow transient external noise to settle.

No blockers from telemetry; I signed off on the CSV and small edits to the runbook.

-Neha
Principal Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, infraops@acmecloud.com
Date: Fri, 05 Jun 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VPC upgrade curation & failsafe brief

Thanks everyone — this looks actionable. Two quick notes from the GTM/SLA side and final confirmation:

1) Customer comms: I'll draft a short advisory that calls out the scheduled window (02:30-06:30 UTC), the canary stages, and the expected transient latency and cache warm-up behaviors. We will offer a 4-hour credit if we exceed the stated SLOs for more than 30 consecutive minutes.

2) SLA exception: approved for this wave to allow hotpatch channel usage for critical fixes only. We will record the agreement in the customer portal and add a note to the incident runbook in case of escalations.

3) Final confirmation request: InfraOps, please confirm the 02:30-06:30 UTC window and your ability to run the net-quiesce checklist and the TCP drain. If you confirm, I will publish the customer advisory and schedule the DocuSign SLA addendum.

Alex — once InfraOps confirms, lock the final runbook changes and I'll coordinate comms + DocuSign.

Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Success (Private)
Redwood Inference
